{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"2b6ec18f553003b3f3065facd6c381057c773bb483e62d2a04eaebefdeb89f02","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:41","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic laws, crossings, lane markings and right of way","heading":"C2 — Traffic laws, crossings, lane markings and right of way","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Traffic laws, crossings, lane markings and right of way

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A06
For a roundabout, use the right approach lane for a right turn and the left for a left turn or U-turn; either approach lane may serve straight travel. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A06
Approach a roundabout to the splitter island’s right and slow to 10–15 mph. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A06
At a roundabout entrance, watch for bicyclists and permit them to merge into the entry lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A06
Yield to pedestrians using the roundabout crosswalk. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A06
Entering drivers must yield to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A06
Within a roundabout, stop only to avoid a collision; circulating traffic has priority over entering traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A06
Travel counterclockwise to the central island’s right, keep speed low and do not pass within the roundabout. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A06
When exiting a roundabout, watch for and yield to both pedestrians and bicyclists. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A06
A diverging diamond interchange temporarily routes traffic on the road’s left side so left turns avoid crossing opposing traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A07
A shared center lane serves left turns and permitted U-turns by traffic traveling in either direction. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A07
Shared-center-lane pavement arrows alternate directions, and its boundaries pair a solid yellow line with a broken yellow line. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A07
A shared center lane can become reversible during rush hours; confirm entry is permitted and safe. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A07
Do not reverse in a travel lane except to parallel park or when necessary to leave a driveway. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A07
After missing a turn or exit, continue to a safe turnaround instead of backing up. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A07
Do not stop in a travel lane for confusion, a breakdown or a passenger; continue until you can safely pull off. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A07
On roads with at least two same-direction lanes, keep right except when passing. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A07
On roads with at least three same-direction lanes and heavy entering or exiting traffic, use the center travel lane. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A07
The far-left lane on a multilane road is intended for passing slower traffic. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A07
Delaware permits passing a left-turning vehicle on the right, but this maneuver demands great caution. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A07
Delaware permits using the shoulder to pass a left-turning vehicle on the right, with extreme care because others may not expect it. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A07
Without turn-control signs or markings, turn from the lane nearest the intended direction into the closest corresponding lane, crossing as few lanes as possible. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A07
Make a turn directly without straying across lane lines or obstructing traffic; change lanes afterward if needed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A07
Avoid swinging left before a right turn or wide into a distant lane while completing it. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A08
Do not cut a left-turn corner sharply into traffic approaching from the left; leave room for opposing left-turners. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A08
Where multiple lanes are designated for a turn, remain in your own lane throughout the turn. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A08
A median opening marked for emergency vehicles only may not be used by ordinary drivers. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A08
When a median crossing is legal and no sign says otherwise, stay to the right of its opening. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R28 | anchor: A08
Whatever the right-of-way situation, do everything possible to avoid striking another vehicle or a pedestrian. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R29 | anchor: A08
Drivers must yield when needed to avoid hitting pedestrians crossing the road. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R30 | anchor: A08
When entering or leaving a driveway, alley or parking lot across a sidewalk, yield to pedestrians. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R31 | anchor: A08
Driving along a sidewalk is illegal; crossing it is the permitted exception. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R32 | anchor: A08
A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane has absolute priority; do not sound the horn and risk confusion or fright. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R33 | anchor: A08
A left-turning driver must yield to opposing vehicles continuing straight. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R34 | anchor: A08
Drivers entering a traffic circle or rotary must give way to those already inside. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R35 | anchor: A08
At an intersection without a stop or yield sign or signal, yield to traffic from the right; the handbook also recommends considering all vehicles before entry. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R36 | anchor: A08
At a four-way stop, the first driver to arrive proceeds first after stopping completely. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R37 | anchor: A08
If vehicles reach a four-way stop together, the one on the right proceeds first. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R38 | anchor: A08
Entering a road from a driveway, alley or roadside requires yielding to traffic on the main road. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R39 | anchor: A08
Vehicles entering from turn-only lanes must yield and stop when necessary. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R40 | anchor: A09
Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without stopping and blocking it. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R41 | anchor: A09
A driver overtaking a same-direction vehicle must yield to that vehicle even if it slows or stops. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R42 | anchor: A09
Yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or flashing red or blue light by moving as far right as possible, following any loudspeaker instructions. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R43 | anchor: A09
If already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection before pulling over. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R44 | anchor: A09
Stop before a school bus loading or unloading children from either direction, except opposing traffic on a highway with at least four lanes, which must still move slowly. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R45 | anchor: A09
A bus’s alternating overhead yellow lights activate about 10 seconds before its flashing red lights; approach carefully and expect a stop. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R46 | anchor: A09
After a bus stops for pupils, wait until its red lights cease and its stop arm retracts before proceeding cautiously. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec09-R47 | anchor: A10
If police, a bus operator or a crossing guard witnesses a school-bus-stop violation and cannot identify the driver, the registered owner is presumed to have committed it. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R48 | anchor: A10
For a first conviction of passing a bus stopped with overhead and stop-arm red lights flashing, the fine is $115 to $230. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R49 | anchor: A10
The same first bus-passing offense may carry 30 to 60 days of imprisonment, alone or with the fine. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R50 | anchor: A10
A similar bus-passing offense within three years carries a fine of $115 to $575. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R51 | anchor: A10
A later similar bus-passing offense within three years also carries imprisonment from 60 days to six months. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R52 | anchor: A10
A first conviction for passing a stopped bus with the described flashing red lights results in a one-month license or driving-privilege suspension. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R53 | anchor: A10
For a second school-bus violation within three years of an earlier violation, the source table gives six months of suspension. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R54 | anchor: A10
The school-bus conviction table gives a one-year suspension for a third or later violation within three years of an earlier violation. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R55 | anchor: A10
For a second school-bus offense, a conditional license may be issued only after at least three months without driving authority. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R56 | anchor: A10
For a third or later school-bus offense, a conditional license may be issued only after at least six months without driving authority. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R57 | anchor: A10
No driving authority is available during the first school-bus offense’s one-month suspension. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R58 | anchor: A10
The handbook’s Red Clay school-bus camera pilot description gives a $100 civil or administrative assessment for a first violation. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R59 | anchor: A10
In that camera-pilot description, each subsequent violation within 10 years has a $500 assessment. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R60 | anchor: A10
The described school district camera pilot may add up to $10 when an assessment remains unpaid for 20 days. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R61 | anchor: A10
The camera-pilot late-payment assessment may rise to at most $20 after 45 days. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R62 | anchor: A10
The camera-pilot late-payment assessment may rise to at most $30 after 90 days. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R63 | anchor: A10
The camera-pilot description permits up to $35 in court or similar administrative costs after an unsuccessful hearing or failure to pay or contest on time. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec09-R64 | anchor: A10
A civilly assessed violation under the described camera pilot is not criminal and does not enter the driving record or insurance determination. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0090]
